name: EchoKit Server
description: Server that powers the EchoKit ESP32 voice device, turning speech into LLM responses and spoken replies, with MCP tool support.
whatItDoes: Acts as the brain for a small open hardware voice assistant, handling the conversation while the device captures and plays audio. Makers can point it at their preferred speech and language model services.
howItWorks: The Rust server receives audio from the device and runs a pipeline of speech recognition, language model and speech synthesis against OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or uses an end-to-end live model such as Gemini Live. A TOML file selects the services and prompts, and MCP servers can be attached for tool use.

requirements.name: EchoKit / ESP32 device
requirements.description: Voice hardware that connects to the server

requirements.name: ASR, LLM and TTS endpoints
requirements.description: Service endpoints and keys set in config.toml

models: OpenAI-compatible ASR, LLM and TTS services; Gemini Live
